summary: Frontend-only validation completed for business plan colour customizer flows on public URL. Colour panel, presets, live colour inputs, and local persistence work. DOCX export works after colour changes. PDF export fails with runtime parsing error triggered by CSS colour functions used in preview styles.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking Download PDF throws runtime error overlay: 'Attempting to parse an unsupported color function "color"' and no downloadable PDF is produced in automation.

integration_issues.issue: html2pdf/html2canvas parser crashes during DOM parsing due unsupported computed color function from CSS, blocking PDF generation.

action_items: Replace or guard unsupported CSS color functions (generated from color-mix usage in preview styles) before HTML is passed to html2canvas/html2pdf.
Retest Download PDF after fallback colours are applied and confirm actual .pdf download on public URL.
Keep DOCX export path unchanged; it currently works after colour changes.
critical_code_review_comments: App.css uses color-mix(...) extensively in business plan preview styles. html2canvas in current PDF pipeline cannot parse resulting computed color() function and throws runtime error.
This is an integration compatibility issue between modern CSS colour functions and client-side PDF renderer; a PDF-safe style fallback layer is required for export path.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Verified on https://freelancer-admin.preview.emergentagent.com/startup/business-plan-generator: customize colours panel visible; coral preset updates preview CSS vars; direct document/font/accent color inputs update preview live and persist after reload; DOCX download works (.docx). Mobile check at 390x844 shows no page-level horizontal overflow (scrollWidth == clientWidth). PDF click consistently logs PAGE ERROR and fails to emit download event.
rca of the issue: Reproduction: open business plan generator, click Download PDF (with default or customized colours). Observed console/page error: 'Attempting to parse an unsupported color function "color"' during DOM parsing. Root cause: preview CSS relies on color-mix(...) in multiple rules, producing computed color() syntax not supported by current html2canvas parser used by html2pdf. Mitigation: export-specific CSS fallback to plain hex/rgb values (or render clone with simplified styles) before invoking PDF generation.
